HypothesizedGapReason: Single-maintainer project paused after finishing a feature. Aaron Robotham made 81 of 83 post-gap commits; last pre-gap commit completed Rfits_pointer loading and no issues were opened during the gap.
WhyRecovered: Maintainer's own research needs: new segim_orig photometry modes, 'Will need this version for the Workshop', and a WAVES survey corner case fix.
WhoRecovered: Same maintainer (Aaron Robotham); only one outside commit (Joel G, 'upgrade cicd').
Notes: ProFound is basically one astronomer's tool, so its activity follows his research schedule. The 6-month gap in 2024 was easy to read: he finished a feature, had no open issues, and came back when he needed new photometry options for a workshop and the WAVES survey. It is still active in 2026.

HypothesizedGapReason: Replaced by OSCAR. PR #206: functionality 'is now available through OSCAR'; co-owner called it 'incompatible with our current philosophy'. Issue #205 (Normaliz segfault, Jul 2023) left unfixed and tests disabled.
WhyRecovered: N/A. The 7 post-gap commits only wind it down: a GAP compatibility fix by Max Horn led to the decision to withdraw it from GAP and update the README.
WhoRecovered: Same people: Martin Bies and GAP maintainer Max Horn, who had also committed before the gap; no new developers.
Notes: The 23-month gap was the start of the end, not a pause. PR #206 says the package was replaced by OSCAR and it was withdrawn from GAP in Jan 2025. The last 7 commits only wind it down, and it is now Inactive.

HypothesizedGapReason: Work shifted to dependent LANL codes. Pre-gap commits were mostly MATAR submodule bumps and merges, so the library was only being kept in sync.
WhyRecovered: MATAR/Kokkos update ('updated matar version (for updated Kokkos)'), then a v2 refactor (#39, Feb 2026) and boundary surface sets 'to be used in fierro'.
WhoRecovered: Mostly new: Jacob Moore made 76 of 90 post-gap commits; existing team (Adrian-Diaz, Nathaniel Morgan, Daniel Dunning) contributed the rest.
Notes: ELEMENTS goes quiet whenever LANL's other codes do not need it, which explains its 3 gaps. The 6-month gap was moderately hard to read since the commits are mostly submodule bumps. It recovered through a Kokkos update and later a v2 refactor led by newcomer Jacob Moore.

HypothesizedGapReason: Research/contest artifact considered finished. Last pre-gap commit adds a DOI to archive it; last issues (#43, #44 from 2021) are open ideas never picked up.
WhyRecovered: N/A. Only one post-gap commit ('Fix missing import', May 2025), a small cleanup.
WhoRecovered: Same person (Márton Elekes) for the single post-gap commit.
Notes: This is a finished research artifact, so its 33-month gap is really the project being done. Adding a DOI right before the gap was the clearest sign. One import fix in 2025 technically makes it Active under the 6-month rule, but it has not recovered.

HypothesizedGapReason: Maintainers busy while user issues piled up (#669 30 comments, #673 23 comments, #675-#682 mostly open) and Python packaging broke (#674 Python 3.12, #687 'CI tests broken').
WhyRecovered: Build modernization to fix broken installs: F95 to F90 rename (Apr 2025), then meson build, NumPy 2.x support, and fixed quippy wheels.
WhoRecovered: Same core maintainers (James Kermode 48, Albert Bartok-Partay 31) plus new contributors (green-br, smjanke) and returning contributor Noam Bernstein.
Notes: QUIP has only one 3+ month gap in 15 years, so the 6-month pause stands out. Issues kept piling up while Python packaging broke, which made the cause fairly clear. The core maintainers came back to modernize the build and are active again with some new contributors.

HypothesizedGapReason: Single maintainer (stevenj) paused after preparing the 1.2.1 release; code was stable and the history was being converted from SVN to git.
WhyRecovered: Moved to git/GitHub ('git conversion', 'add mailmap file', Mar 2014); outside users opened issues #1-#7 within weeks, creating demand.
WhoRecovered: Same maintainer restarted it (stevenj = Steven G. Johnson); new people (Ardavan Oskooi, Chris Hogan, Homer Reid) drove later growth.
Notes: Meep went from a one-person project with 8 gaps to a busy multi-developer project. The 15-month gap was hard to read from commits alone, but the post-gap git conversion and new GitHub issues show the move to GitHub is what brought it back. It is very active today.

HypothesizedGapReason: Single developer finished a docs/release push ('add newest version', README edits) and stopped.
WhyRecovered: Moved to the opticspy repo with a new partner (issues 'Init repository', 'Invite more members', 'build linux wheels', Jan 2017) and FFTW3-accelerated builds.
WhoRecovered: Same developer (Fred van Goor) plus a new contributor (guyskk) who set up wheels and CI.
Notes: LightPipes is a one-developer project with 9 gaps, so it moves in bursts. The 12-month gap in 2016 was easy to read: a docs/release push ended and nothing came in until a new partner helped move it to the opticspy repo. It is still updated occasionally.

HypothesizedGapReason: Package released to CRAN and considered done (pre-gap commits are all CRAN submission prep). Issue #19 went unanswered 6 months because the maintainer 'did not get any emails from this repo'.
WhyRecovered: External PR #20 'Update deprecated syntax for future rstan compatibility' (Sep 2023) forced an update, followed by CMD check and CI fixes.
WhoRecovered: Same people: Philippe Rast (18 of 19) and Andrew Johnson, who also contributed before the gap.
Notes: bmgarch goes quiet after each CRAN release. The 20-month gap was easy to read because the maintainer admitted missing issue notifications, and an outside rstan compatibility PR brought it back. It is active again with a v2.1.0 release in 2026.

WhyRecovered: Normal work resumed after a 2-month pause: Moodle 4.1 tests and the 8.0.0 release.
WhoRecovered: Same company team (carla-at-wiris, icaparros-at-wiris, Xavier Ripoll).
Notes: This company-maintained plugin has no 3+ month gaps, so it counts as always active. Its longest pause was 2 months over the 2022 summer, and work resumed with the normal Moodle 4.1 and 8.0.0 release cycle.

HypothesizedGapReason: Short review backlog: PR #823 opened Dec 2024 was not merged until Jun 2025, Dependabot PR #822 still open, issues #824-#826 had no replies during the gap.
WhyRecovered: Newcomer PR #828 fixed issue #826, then the maintainer merged the backlog (#823, #828, #829, #830) on 2025-06-09.
WhoRecovered: Mostly existing team (Tadas Tamosauskas, Joko Triono) plus newcomer Good-soup1.
Notes: SequenceServer has a cyclical pattern of short pauses. Its 4-month gap was a review backlog where PRs and issues waited without replies. It recovered when a newcomer fixed an issue and a maintainer merged the queue in June 2025.
